issues.t: Head gasket leak and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant keeps disappearing, the engine runs hot, steam or white smoke, oil or coolant leaks, and sometimes a sudden loss of power.
issues.why: Head gaskets on the older 2.2L and 2.4L engines are a common failure, often made worse by overheating. Owners also report warped or cracked heads and leaking plastic coolant fittings on the head.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. Ask for a cooling system pressure test and a combustion leak test, and check that the cooling fan runs.

issues.t: Engine knock that leads to engine failure
issues.sym: A knocking noise, at first only when cold or at certain engine speeds, that gets worse until the engine fails.
issues.why: Owners report piston knock, broken connecting rods and failed lifters on early Sunfires, some at 47,000 to 72,000 miles.
issues.next: Have any new engine knock checked right away and check the oil level often. Catching it early can save the engine.

issues.t: Water pump leak on the 2.4L
issues.sym: Coolant drips and a coolant level that keeps dropping.
issues.why: The 2.4L Twin Cam's water pump is mounted inside the front of the engine and driven by the timing chain, so a leak means a long, involved repair.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up and don't let it overheat. Ask for a quote that includes timing chain parts while the front of the engine is open.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle or failure on the 2.2L Ecotec
issues.sym: Rattle or knock at startup or idle, misfires, rough idle, poor running or a no-start.
issues.why: Early 2.2L Ecotec engines starved the timing chain tensioner of oil at idle, so it wore out. Low oil makes it worse.
issues.next: Keep the oil full and changed on time. If you hear a rattle, get it checked before the chain skips and damages the engine.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Stalling in traffic, cranks but won't start, or hesitation before it dies.
issues.why: The in-tank electric fuel pump fails on these cars, with reports from about 53,000 to 122,000 miles.
issues.next: If it cranks but won't start, have fuel pressure checked. A tow is safer than trying to keep restarting it in traffic.

issues.t: Engine stalls while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out at idle, while turning or on the highway, then usually restarts. Some cars stall only in hot weather.
issues.why: Owners report stalling that shops often can't reproduce. Fuel pumps were replaced in some cases; others suspected electrical contacts or the engine computer.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Note when it stalls (hot, idle, turning) and whether any lights come on. Stalling cuts power steering and brake assist, so get it diagnosed soon.

issues.t: Instrument cluster gauges go haywire
issues.sym: The speedometer, tachometer, fuel or temperature gauge sticks, jumps or stops working.
issues.why: Small stepper motors that move the gauge needles fail inside the instrument cluster.
issues.next: A cluster repair shop can often replace the stepper motors for less than a new cluster. Don't trust the speedometer until it's fixed.

issues.t: Headlights stop working
issues.sym: Headlights or running lights flicker, go out while driving, or work only on high beam.
issues.why: Owners report corroded wires in the front wiring harness, plus headlight failures on earlier years.
issues.next: Driving without headlights at night is dangerous. Have the front harness and headlight switch checked for corrosion.

issues.t: Power window motor fails
issues.sym: A window moves slowly, stops partway or won't move at all.
issues.why: Window motors overheat and wear out, and the regulators also fail.
issues.next: Have the switch, motor and regulator checked. A window stuck down should be fixed before rain or theft becomes a problem.

issues.t: Turn signals stop working
issues.sym: One or both turn signals don't flash or work only some of the time.
issues.why: The turn signal switch in the steering column can fail.
issues.next: Use hand signals if needed and have the flasher, bulbs and switch checked. The switch is a common, moderate repair.

issues.t: Vent mode control stuck on one setting
issues.sym: Air comes out of only one set of vents, the defroster won't work, or the knob turns but nothing changes.
issues.why: The vent mode cable or a plastic part inside the heater box breaks or jams.
issues.next: A working defroster matters for safety in winter. Have the mode cable and door checked; the parts sit deep in the dash.

issues.t: ABS acts up or wheels lock in the rain
issues.sym: The ABS light comes on, the ABS pulses or feels like it lets go on wet roads, or a wheel locks up.
issues.why: Owners of these years report ABS problems in wet weather and ABS failures. Wheel speed sensors, rotors and the ABS unit are the usual suspects.
issues.next: Leave extra room in the rain. Have the ABS codes read and the wheel speed sensors and brakes inspected.

issues.t: Passlock anti-theft no-start
issues.sym: The security light flashes and the car won't start, won't shut off, or the shifter won't leave Park.
issues.why: The Passlock anti-theft system can reject the ignition key, often because of a worn ignition lock cylinder or sensor.
issues.next: Try waiting 10 minutes with the key on, then restart. If it keeps happening, have the ignition cylinder and Passlock sensor tested.

issues.t: Clear coat peels off the paint
issues.sym: Patches of paint turn chalky and the clear top layer flakes away, often on the roof, hood and trunk.
issues.why: Owners report the clear coat breaking down around 59,000 miles.
issues.next: Wash and wax often to slow it down. A repaint of the damaged panels is the only real fix.

issues.t: Clutch slave cylinder leaks
issues.sym: The clutch pedal goes soft or to the floor and shifting gets hard.
issues.why: On manual-transmission cars the hydraulic slave cylinder can leak fluid.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid level. Have the slave cylinder replaced before the clutch stops releasing.

issues.t: Wiring harness shorts out
issues.sym: Electrical items fail or act up, sometimes with a burning smell.
issues.why: Owners report wiring harness shorts that can be hard to fix.
issues.next: If you smell burning plastic or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off, get everyone out and away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until the wiring has been repaired. Then have the wiring inspected.

issues.t: Automatic transmission won't engage or leaks fluid
issues.sym: The car won't go into gear, or transmission fluid drips from the pan.
issues.why: Owners report the transmission not engaging at high mileage and pan seal leaks around 50,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level often. A pan gasket is a simple fix; a transmission that won't engage needs a full diagnosis.

issues.t: Trunk latch won't open
issues.sym: The trunk won't open with the key or button.
issues.why: Owners report trunk latch failures at low mileage.
issues.next: Have the latch, release cable and switch checked.

issues.t: Ignition switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the steering column, even with the engine off.
issues.why: GM recalled these cars because a damaged ignition switch could overheat and start a fire in the steering column.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Steering can get hard to turn (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly takes much more effort, like a car without power steering.
issues.why: The power steering pinion shaft could move inside the steering gear. GM recalled over a million cars to inspect it.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Rear suspension can fail (recall)
issues.sym: No early warning; a loss of control is possible.
issues.why: GM recalled these cars for a rear suspension defect that could cause a loss of vehicle control.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Airbags deploy with too much force (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: GM recalled these cars because the airbags deployed with high force that could hurt people sitting too close.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free. Sit well back from the steering wheel and dash.

issues.t: Interior lights turn on by themselves (recall)
issues.sym: The dome lights come on unexpectedly while driving.
issues.why: A lighting control fault could switch on interior lights and startle the driver.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Hazard lights may not flash (recall)
issues.sym: The four-way flashers don't blink.
issues.why: GM recalled these cars because the hazard flashers might not work when needed.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Wheel can come off from loose lug nuts (recall)
issues.sym: Wheel wobble or clunking, then possible wheel separation.
issues.why: GM recalled some cars because the wheel lug nuts could loosen and a wheel could come off.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Dash lights may not light at night (recall)
issues.sym: The instrument panel stays dark at night.
issues.why: A fault on some 1999 cars left the instrument panel unlit at night.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Brake lights and turn signals can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights or rear turn signals don't light.
issues.why: GM recalled these cars because the rear bulb sockets could fail.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Rear seat belt anchor can separate (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: On a small number of cars the passenger-side rear seat belt upper anchor might separate in a severe crash.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.
